sections.label: PM on extra paternity leave
sections.summary: The Prime Minister said eligible fathers may get an extra week of paid paternity leave with employer approval.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: During last year's National Day Rally (NDR), our Prime Minister said that eligible fathers may be granted an extra week of paid paternity leave, with their employers' approval.

sections.label: Jubilee year paternity leave extension
sections.summary: The extra week of paid leave was extended to all fathers of Singaporean babies born on or after 1 January 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: To celebrate the Jubilee year, we had extended the extra week of paid leave to all fathers of Singaporean babies born on or after 1 January 2015.

sections.label: Paternity leave mandate and CDA benefits
sections.summary: Josephine Teo announced the second week of paternity leave will be mandated from 1 January 2017, and CDA benefits extended to unwed parents' children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Members will also remember Senior Minister of State Josephine Teo announcing at the National Population and Talent Division's (NPTD) Committee of Supply (COS) last month that this second week of paternity leave will be mandated from 1 January 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Separately, as announced at my Ministry's COS last month, we will extend the Child Development Account (CDA) benefits to Singaporean children of unwed parents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: This includes the $3,000 CDA First Step grant.

sections.label: Unwed mothers maternity leave
sections.summary: Unwed mothers will qualify for the full 16 weeks of maternity leave for children born from early next year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Unwed mothers will also qualify for the full 16 weeks of maternity leave for children born from early next year.

sections.label: Lowest citizen births in 2010
sections.summary: In 2010, citizen births hit their lowest number at just over 30,000 babies born.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In 2010, we hit our lowest number of citizen births at just over 30,000 babies born.

sections.label: Citizen births and fertility rate
sections.summary: Last year citizen births almost hit 34,000, the highest in a decade, with the TFR around 1.25.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In fact, last year, citizen births almost hit 34,000 babies, the highest in a decade.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The total fertility rate (TFR) is hovering around 1.25, off the low of 1.16 in 2010.

sections.label: CDA matching and First Step grant
sections.summary: Middle-income families with three children need $24,000 in CDA for full matching, and the $3,000 First Step grant addresses inequality.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Middle-income families just managing to make ends meet to support three children would need to lock up $24,000 in CDA to reap the full benefits of dollar-for-dollar matching from the Government.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The new CDA First Step grant of $3,000 addresses this issue of inequality.

sections.label: Additional Child Care Subsidy for fathers
sections.summary: The Additional Child Care Subsidy for working mothers should be gender-neutral and extended to working fathers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Additional Child Care Subsidy for working mothers should be made gender-neutral and extended to working fathers, so that lower-income female homemakers with several children or elderly dependants are not denied the subsidy and could provide better care to the dependants.

sections.label: CDA and Baby Bonus for unwed parents
sections.summary: Extending CDA co-savings eligibility to single unwed parents' children is a first step, with Baby Bonus Cash Gift extension next.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Extending eligibility for the CDA co-savings grant to the children of single unwed parents is a good first step.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The next step is to consider extending the Baby Bonus Cash Gift to the same children, but perhaps to be deposited into the CDA so that the grant may be locked up for the sole benefit of the children.

sections.label: Foreign spouses citizenship priority
sections.summary: The Government should alleviate stress of Singaporean spouses and children, and WP calls for priority naturalisation for foreign spouses after five years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government should alleviate the stress and separation anxieties faced by the Singaporean spouses and children in such situations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I reiterate WP's call for foreign spouses of Singapore Citizens to be given priority for citizenship naturalisation after five years on the Long-Term Visit Pass Plus.

sections.label: Standardised $10,000 CDA allocation
sections.summary: The Government should automatically allocate a standardised $10,000 to the CDA for each child.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government should bring this policy move to its logical conclusion by automatically allocating to the CDA a standardised $10,000 for each child.

sections.label: Equalising grants for children
sections.summary: Bigger grants for existing children would alleviate stress and encourage family life, and equalising grants would remove inequality, as equality matters for pro-birth policy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Giving a bigger grant for the existing children would alleviate the immediate stress, encourage a healthy family life and persuade parents that it is worth the while to have a third child and more.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Equalising the grants would also remove an artificial inequality within the family created by the policy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: With the current policy, the third and fourth child could receive up to $12,000 more savings and grants, compared to the first and second child, and the fifth child onwards could receive up to $24,000 more.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This means that the older children would have less funds benefiting their education and well-being, compared to the younger children.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As the lessons of three decades show, the Government cannot be reactive towards lower birth rates and should be proactive to aim for higher birth rates.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: And as the Government seeks to enable and empower Singaporeans to have more babies, please remember these two words as a key principle to guide pro-birth policy: equality matters.

sections.label: Child Development Co-Savings Scheme expansion
sections.summary: The proposed amendment to section 3 expands the categories of children eligible under the Child Development Co-Savings Scheme, so children other than those of married mothers now qualify.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We must help and support them rather than penalise them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, I am extremely delighted that the proposed amendment to section 3 seeks to expand the categories of children who may be eligible under the Child Development Co-Savings Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Children, other than children of married mothers, will now qualify for the scheme.

sections.label: Paternity leave reimbursement amendments
sections.summary: The Bill allows employers to claim reimbursement from the Government for the extra week of paternity leave, and later amendments will legislate a second week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And the researcher's advice was simple, and I quote again, "Try to get leave from work in order to spend as much time as possible with your child during his first year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But, above all, make sure you spend high quality time with your child." The amendments in this Bill seek to provide this by allowing employers to claim reimbursement from the Government for the extra week of paternity leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Subsequent amendments to this Act, as the Minister has mentioned, where the second week of paternity leave will be legislated, will further strengthen this.

sections.label: Deputy Prime Minister on birth rate
sections.summary: The Deputy Prime Minister said in his opening remarks on 4 February 2013 that he hoped the birth rate could increase to at least 1.4 or 1.5.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: In fact, in the Deputy Prime Minister's opening remarks at the Parliamentary debate on the Population White Paper on 4 February 2013, he said, "In the short term, I hope our birth rate can increase to at least 1.4 or 1.5", which was our birth rate not so long ago, around the late-1990s and the early-2000s.

sections.label: Support for unwed parents' children
sections.summary: The speaker is heartened by Mr Louis Ng and Assoc Prof Daniel Goh's support for extending the Child Development Co-Saving Scheme to children of unwed parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Societal attitudes really are a sum total of individual attitudes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: I am also very heartened to hear from both Mr Louis Ng and Assoc Prof Daniel Goh on their support of the extension of the Child Development Co-Saving Scheme to children of unwed parents.

sections.label: Benefits and leave eligibility
sections.summary: Benefits include education, healthcare subsidies, MediSave grant for newborns, infant and childcare subsidies and foreign domestic worker levy concession, and all working parents are eligible for infant care and childcare leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: For example, the benefits include education, healthcare subsidies, MediSave grant for newborns, centre-based infant and childcare subsidies and foreign domestic worker levy concession.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: All working parents, regardless of their marital status, are also eligible for infant care leave, childcare leave before the child turns seven, and extended childcare leave when the child is seven to 12 years old.

sections.label: Government funding for paternity leave
sections.summary: Employers who grant this leave have the Government's support, and the Government will fully fund it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: For the employers who have been doing so, you have the Government's support; we will fully fund this leave, as long as you grant it.

sections.label: Government support for parenthood
sections.summary: The Government will support parents through leave schemes, pro-family workplaces and family-friendly employer practices, and the amendments support parenthood.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: The Government will do its part by continuing to support parents through leave schemes and promoting a pro-family workplace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: This includes encouraging employers to adopt family-friendly practices, such as providing flexible work arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: The amendments tabled today are in support of parenthood.
